This performance is not only accelerating [E58] but also vastly outstrips the sector median profit growth of 10.5% [E66]. Consequently, the company is beginning to outperform market expectations, as profit growth has recently exceeded one-year price growth by 145% [E48]. Furthermore, the company has failed to generate long-term value for shareholders, with compounded profit growth over the last decade at -10% [E14] and a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. The bear focuses on historical stagnation, yet ignores the critical inflection point in the company's performance [E16]. While the bear cites long-term profit decline [E14], it fails to acknowledge that current profit growth of 108% [E16] is ten times the sector median of 10.5% [E66]. This acceleration is not merely a statistical outlier but a fundamental shift, as evidenced by the scanX signal engine identifying that profit growth now significantly outpaces price growth [E48]. Conceded: [E12, E13, E21, E22, E23, E24] confirm a history of low returns, but these metrics are backward-looking and fail to capture the momentum indicated by the earnings growth acceleration [E58]. Trading at a deep discount of 0.31x book value [E7] provides a massive margin of safety for investors betting on this recent turnaround. The bear’s reliance on the 1080 P/E [E1] is misleading, as it ignores the 0x P/E valuation relative to the sector benchmark [E6], suggesting the market has yet to price in the company's newfound profitability [E56].

The bull’s reliance on a single year of profit growth [E16] ignores the overwhelming evidence of long-term value destruction, specifically the 10-year compounded profit growth of -10% [E14] and a decade of stagnant returns [E21]. While the bull highlights a recent 108% profit increase [E16], this must be weighed against the fact that the company’s median return on equity over 3, 5, and 10 years remains 0% [E21, E22, E23]. Conceded: [E16, E56, E58] indicate a recent uptick in earnings, but this momentum is contradicted by the company’s inability to generate any return on capital, as evidenced by an ROCE of 0.0% [E12]. The bull’s argument regarding the P/E ratio is internally inconsistent, as the company trades at an extreme 1080x P/E [E1], which suggests that the market is already pricing in significant future expectations that the company has historically failed to meet [E14, E24]. Furthermore, the lack of any dividend yield [E4] provides no compensation for investors while they wait for this supposed turnaround to materialize. The low price-to-book ratio [E2, E7] is not a margin of safety but a reflection of the company’s persistent failure to generate meaningful returns on its assets [E8, E53, E59].
